text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament's public funds protection committee wants missile purchase plan debated. Experts say the deal to buy British Aerospace Sea Skua missiles could be worth up to $150 million. MPs fear irregularities in defence contracts.
- Kuwait to cut medicine price by five to 15 percent, official says.
- Value of shares traded on the Kuwait Stock Exchange in June totalled 682.9 million dinars ($2.239 billion).

- Parliamentary panel approves a bill to compensate Kuwaitis keeping farms near the border areas. Newspapers have often reported raids by Iraqi gunmen on farms on the Kuwaiti side of the Iraq-Kuwait border. The measure aims at closing the farms.
- Acting Prime Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah chairs a meeting of the Supreme Petroleum Council.
- Citizens urge ministry to hit hard at commercial cheating.
- Iraqi President Saddam Hussein should face war crime tribunal, British MP says.

- Effects of the 1991 environmental catastrophe continue, expert says. Some 700 oil wells were torched or damaged during the 1991 Gulf War which ended a seven-month Iraqi occupation of the tiny Gulf state.
